sources.entry: AppFlowy - Build detailed lists of to-do’s for different projects while tracking the status of each one. Open Source Notion Alternative. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Rust/Dart/Docker
AppFlowy | Open-source Notion alternative with a focus on privacy and extensibility.

summary.one_liner: AppFlowy is an open-source, Flutter and Rust desktop and mobile workspace app that positions itself as an alternative to Notion.
summary.what_it_does: The README presents AppFlowy as an AI workspace and open-source alternative to Notion, with a focus on data privacy and native cross-platform experience. It lists desktop downloads for macOS, Windows, and Linux, plus other channels including FlatHub, Snapcraft, and SourceForge. It is also listed as available on the iPhone App Store and on the Play Store for Android 10 or above. The README mentions a self-hosting option but does not describe its setup in the text provided. The project is built with Flutter and Rust, and the README points to separate documentation for OS-specific development setup, roadmap, and contribution guidelines. Translations are maintained as JSON files under frontend/resources/translations. The metadata lists to-do list and project status tracking as a use case.
use_cases: Notion alternative for notes and knowledge management
private team workspace with data under own control
cross-platform note-taking on desktop and mobile
building custom collaborative apps from building blocks
how_to_run: Download AppFlowy Desktop for macOS, Windows, or Linux from the project's releases
Install from FlatHub, Snapcraft, or SourceForge
Install the iPhone app from the App Store or the Android app from the Play Store (Android 10+)
For self-hosting or development, follow the OS-specific documentation linked from the README
notable: Positions itself as an open-source Notion alternative with a focus on data privacy
Single codebase in Flutter and Rust targeting multiple platforms
Offers a self-hosting option according to the README
Translations handled via JSON files and the inlang editor
caveats: ARMv7 Android devices are not supported
README states the project does not claim to outperform Notion in functionality or design, at least for now
Self-hosting and development setup details are delegated to separate documentation not included in the README
